reference_policy: Immutable logical contract. The reference source digests below identify the initial implementation; they are not refreshed when a compatible node adapter is rebuilt or replaced. Retained definitions require these exact contract bytes. Artifact provenance separately records the implementation actually shipped.
reference_revision_note: K3 additions are identified by the source digests, relative to this baseline. The introducing Git commit preserves the complete reference sources.

semantics.ordering: Keys are BLOB paths ordered lexicographically by bytes. Range lower bounds preserve their inclusive/exclusive flag, upper bounds are exclusive, and descending traversal reverses the same live set. Selected row metadata and value refer to the same stored version.
semantics.liveness: The greatest-height version of each contract/path determines liveness. A tombstone hides all older values. Same-height replacement refreshes value and size; older inserts cannot resurrect a newer tombstone. Current-state indices are derived and repaired on rollback.
semantics.visibility: Ordinary storage callbacks share the owned writer connection and observe earlier writes in that transaction. Native identities, contract artifacts, nonces, metadata, and inspection preserve the callback shapes and behavior of the reference implementation.
semantics.values: Metadata reads precede budgeted value reads. Stored size and selected value must remain consistent. Cursor ownership is adapter-specific; a cursor from a different adapter is rejected. Storage callbacks preserve absence, errors, and row ordering rather than substituting empty values.
semantics.errors: Preserve callback result classification and observable error rendering from the reference implementation. SQL/driver failures are not converted to successful absence. A shared driver upgrade requires compatibility evidence for every retained contract, including affected errors.
semantics.transactions: Canonical effects use an owned BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. Nested SAVEPOINT S{index}, RELEASE, and ROLLBACK TO preserve ordered effects. Root rollback undoes state, checkpoint, accounting, and journal changes together. Unsettled or failed cleanup quarantines the owner rather than admitting reuse.
semantics.accounting: Depositor footprint is derived from latest live deposits with checked accounting in the retained implementation. Tombstones and replacements adjust the footprint; rollback and repair preserve the same totals. Nested rollback does not refund migration work already consumed.
semantics.checkpoints: Each contract_state insertion chains the ordered row digest into the current checkpoint using the exact field serialization and hash construction in checkpoint_trigger.sql. Same-height writes update that height in effect order. Rollback restores the earlier chain; merely pruning invisible historical rows does not add checkpoint effects.
semantics.migration_input: A dedicated query-only connection pins the pre-migration snapshot after the writer reservation and an actual lineage/anchor query. Point reads and ordered scans continue to see that snapshot while writes proceed. Metadata is returned before bounded chunks of at most 65536 bytes; handles belong to one root and are revoked on cleanup, including failed cleanup. Required work is charged before access, with five dimensions and sticky exhaustion in the retained context.
